    fn check_layer_kinds(&self, fields: &Fields) -> Result<(), EngError> {
        // The pinned reference derives the order from the interval alone and defaults the
        // interval to 4 (qwen3_5.py:43,203). A present layer_types must equal that order.
        let interval = fields
            .optional_u32("full_attention_interval")?
            .unwrap_or(DEFAULT_FULL_ATTENTION_INTERVAL);
        if interval == 0 {
            return Err(EngError::Checkpoint(
                "configuration full_attention_interval must exceed zero".into(),
            ));
        }
        let derived: Vec<AttentionKind> = (1..=fields
            .expect_u32("num_hidden_layers", self.layers)?)
            .map(|position| {
                if position % interval == 0 {
                    AttentionKind::Full
                } else {
                    AttentionKind::DeltaNet
                }
            })
            .collect();
        let declared: Vec<AttentionKind> = self
            .layers_attention
            .iter()
            .map(|kind| config_layer_kind(*kind))
            .collect();
        if derived != declared {
            return Err(EngError::Checkpoint(format!(
                "configuration full_attention_interval {interval} gives a layer order that differs from family {}",
                self.name
            )));
        }
        match fields.object.get("layer_types") {
            None => Ok(()),
            Some(Value::Array(types)) => {
                let listed = types
                    .iter()
                    .map(|kind| match kind.as_str() {
                        Some("linear_attention") => Ok(AttentionKind::DeltaNet),
                        Some("full_attention") => Ok(AttentionKind::Full),
                        _ => Err(EngError::Checkpoint(format!(
                            "configuration layer_types entry {kind} is unsupported"
                        ))),
                    })
                    .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
                if listed == derived {
                    Ok(())
                } else {
                    Err(EngError::Checkpoint(format!(
                        "configuration layer_types differ from the order that full_attention_interval {interval} gives, family {}",
                        self.name
                    )))
                }
            }
            Some(_) => Err(EngError::Checkpoint(
                "configuration layer_types must be an array".into(),
            )),
        }
    }

    fn check_linear(&self, fields: &Fields) -> Result<(), EngError> {
        let Some(linear) = self.linear else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        fields.expect_u32("linear_num_key_heads", linear.key_heads)?;
        fields.expect_u32("linear_key_head_dim", linear.key_head_dim)?;
        fields.expect_u32("linear_num_value_heads", linear.value_heads)?;
        fields.expect_u32("linear_value_head_dim", linear.value_head_dim)?;
        fields.expect_u32("linear_conv_kernel_dim", linear.conv_kernel)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    fn check_quantization(&self, config: &[u8]) -> Result<(), EngError> {
        let defaults = QuantizationMap::from_json(config)?.defaults();
        if defaults.mode != QuantizationMode::Affine
            || defaults.bits != self.quant_bits
            || defaults.group_size != self.quant_group
        {
            return Err(EngError::Checkpoint(format!(
                "configuration quantization is {:?} {} bits in groups of {}, family {} declares affine {} bits in groups of {}",
                defaults.mode,
                defaults.bits,
                defaults.group_size,
                self.name,
                self.quant_bits,
                self.quant_group
            )));
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// The configuration vocabulary distinguishes only `full_attention` and
/// `linear_attention`. A family executes the full-attention positions either as
/// `AttentionKind::Full` or as the sparse `AttentionKind::Qsa`, so both declare
/// the same configuration kind.
fn config_layer_kind(kind: AttentionKind) -> AttentionKind {
    match kind {
        AttentionKind::Full | AttentionKind::Qsa => AttentionKind::Full,
        AttentionKind::DeltaNet => AttentionKind::DeltaNet,
    }
}

struct Fields<'a> {
    family: &'static str,
    object: &'a Value,
}

impl Fields<'_> {
    fn reject(&self, name: &str) -> Result<(), EngError> {
        if self.object.get(name).is_some() {
            return Err(EngError::Checkpoint(format!(
                "configuration {name} is not used by family {}",
                self.family
            )));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn optional_u32(&self, name: &str) -> Result<Option<u32>, EngError> {
        let Some(value) = self.object.get(name) else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        value
            .as_u64()
            .and_then(|number| u32::try_from(number).ok())
            .map(Some)
            .ok_or_else(|| {
                EngError::Checkpoint(format!("configuration {name} must be a u32 integer"))
            })
    }

    fn u32(&self, name: &str) -> Result<u32, EngError> {
        self.optional_u32(name)?
            .ok_or_else(|| EngError::Checkpoint(format!("configuration lacks {name}")))
    }

    fn string(&self, name: &str) -> Result<&str, EngError> {
        self.object
            .get(name)
            .ok_or_else(|| EngError::Checkpoint(format!("configuration lacks {name}")))?
            .as_str()
            .ok_or_else(|| EngError::Checkpoint(format!("configuration {name} must be a string")))
    }

    fn optional_bool(&self, name: &str) -> Result<Option<bool>, EngError> {
        match self.object.get(name) {
            None => Ok(None),
            Some(Value::Bool(flag)) => Ok(Some(*flag)),
            Some(_) => Err(EngError::Checkpoint(format!(
                "configuration {name} must be a boolean"
            ))),
        }
    }

    fn f64(&self, name: &str) -> Result<f64, EngError> {
        self.object
            .get(name)
            .ok_or_else(|| EngError::Checkpoint(format!("configuration lacks {name}")))?
            .as_f64()
            .ok_or_else(|| EngError::Checkpoint(format!("configuration {name} must be a number")))
    }

    /// Reads `rope_parameters.rope_theta`, the only source the reference uses
    /// (`qwen3_5.py:54-61,72-82`). A missing nested value makes the reference fall back to
    /// 1e5, so the check rejects it. A top-level copy must agree with the nested value.
    fn rope_theta(&self) -> Result<f64, EngError> {
        let nested = self
            .object
            .get("rope_parameters")
            .and_then(|parameters| parameters.get("rope_theta"))
            .ok_or_else(|| {
                EngError::Checkpoint("configuration lacks rope_parameters.rope_theta".into())
            })?
            .as_f64()
            .ok_or_else(|| {
                EngError::Checkpoint("configuration rope_theta must be a number".into())
            })?;
        if let Some(top) = self.object.get("rope_theta")
            && top.as_f64() != Some(nested)
        {
            return Err(EngError::Checkpoint(format!(
                "configuration rope_theta {top} disagrees with rope_parameters.rope_theta {nested}"
            )));
        }
        Ok(nested)
    }

    fn expect_u32(&self, name: &str, declared: u32) -> Result<u32, EngError> {
        let found = self.u32(name)?;
        self.mismatch(name, Some(u64::from(found)), u64::from(declared))?;
        Ok(found)
    }

    fn mismatch(&self, name: &str, found: Option<u64>, declared: u64) -> Result<(), EngError> {
        match found {
            Some(found) if found == declared => Ok(()),
            Some(found) => Err(self.differs(name, found, declared)),
            None => Err(EngError::Checkpoint(format!(
                "configuration {name} cannot be derived for family {}",
                self.family
            ))),
        }
    }

    fn differs(
        &self,
        name: &str,
        found: impl std::fmt::Display,
        declared: impl std::fmt::Display,
    ) -> EngError {
        EngError::Checkpoint(format!(
            "configuration {name} is {found}, family {} declares {declared}",
            self.family
        ))
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::family::spec::{QWEN3_6_35B_A3B, QWEN3_8_27B_DENSE};
    use serde_json::json;

    #[test]
    fn exl3_architecture_is_checked_without_mlx_quantization() {
        let mut config: Value = serde_json::from_slice(include_bytes!(
            "../../tests/fixtures/qwen3_6_35b_a3b_config.json"
        ))
        .unwrap();
        config.as_object_mut().unwrap().remove("quantization");
        config["quantization_config"] = json!({"quant_method": "exl3", "version": "1.4.9"});
        let bytes = config.to_string();
        crate::weights::exl3::Config::from_json(bytes.as_bytes()).expect("supported EXL3 format");
        QWEN3_6_35B_A3B
            .check_architecture_config(bytes.as_bytes())
            .expect("Qwen architecture must not require MLX affine quantization");
        assert!(matches!(
            QWEN3_6_35B_A3B.check_config(bytes.as_bytes()),
            Err(EngError::Checkpoint(message))
                if message.contains("quant_method is not MLX quantization metadata")
        ));
        config["text_config"]["hidden_size"] = json!(1);
        assert!(matches!(
            QWEN3_6_35B_A3B.check_architecture_config(config.to_string().as_bytes()),
            Err(EngError::Checkpoint(message)) if message.contains("hidden_size")
        ));
    }

    // Checkpoint fields supplied by the qualification owner, not generated from FamilySpec.
    fn dense_config() -> Value {
        json!({
            "model_type": "qwen3_5",
            "quantization": {"mode": "affine", "bits": 6, "group_size": 64},
            "text_config": {
                "model_type": "qwen3_5_text",
                "hidden_size": 5120, "intermediate_size": 17408,
                "num_hidden_layers": 64, "num_attention_heads": 24,
                "num_key_value_heads": 4, "head_dim": 256, "vocab_size": 248320,
                "max_position_embeddings": 262144, "full_attention_interval": 4,
                "attn_output_gate": true, "tie_word_embeddings": false,
                "attention_bias": false, "hidden_act": "silu", "rms_norm_eps": 1e-6,
                "linear_num_key_heads": 16, "linear_key_head_dim": 128,
                "linear_num_value_heads": 48, "linear_value_head_dim": 128,
                "linear_conv_kernel_dim": 4,
                "rope_parameters": {
                    "rope_theta": 10000000, "partial_rotary_factor": 0.25,
                    "mrope_interleaved": true, "mrope_section": [11, 11, 10]
                },
                "layer_types": (0..64).map(|i| if i % 4 == 3 {
                    "full_attention"
                } else {
                    "linear_attention"
                }).collect::<Vec<_>>()
            }
        })
    }

    #[test]
    fn dense_checkpoint_text_config_passes() {
        QWEN3_8_27B_DENSE
            .check_config(dense_config().to_string().as_bytes())
            .expect("dense checkpoint dimensions");
    }

    #[test]
    fn dense_dimensions_and_hybrid_order_are_checked() {
        for field in [
            "hidden_size",
            "intermediate_size",
            "num_hidden_layers",
            "num_attention_heads",
            "num_key_value_heads",
            "head_dim",
            "vocab_size",
            "max_position_embeddings",
            "full_attention_interval",
            "linear_num_key_heads",
            "linear_key_head_dim",
            "linear_num_value_heads",
            "linear_value_head_dim",
            "linear_conv_kernel_dim",
        ] {
            let mut config = dense_config();
            config["text_config"][field] = json!(1);
            assert!(
                QWEN3_8_27B_DENSE
                    .check_config(config.to_string().as_bytes())
                    .is_err(),
                "{field}"
            );
        }
        let mut config = dense_config();
        config["text_config"]["layer_types"][0] = json!("full_attention");
        assert!(
            QWEN3_8_27B_DENSE
                .check_config(config.to_string().as_bytes())
                .is_err()
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn dense_config_requires_model_type_and_intermediate_size() {
        for field in ["model_type", "intermediate_size"] {
            let mut config = dense_config();
            config["text_config"].as_object_mut().unwrap().remove(field);
            assert!(
                QWEN3_8_27B_DENSE
                    .check_config(config.to_string().as_bytes())
                    .is_err()
            );
        }
        let mut config = dense_config();
        config["model_type"] = json!("qwen3_5_moe");
        assert!(
            QWEN3_8_27B_DENSE
                .check_config(config.to_string().as_bytes())
                .is_err()
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn dense_config_rejects_moe_fields_and_moe_config_tolerates_intermediate_size() {
        for field in [
            "num_experts",
            "num_experts_per_tok",
            "moe_intermediate_size",
            "shared_expert_intermediate_size",
            "norm_topk_prob",
        ] {
            let mut config = dense_config();
            config["text_config"][field] = json!(0);
            assert!(
                QWEN3_8_27B_DENSE
                    .check_config(config.to_string().as_bytes())
                    .is_err()
            );
        }
        let mut config: Value = serde_json::from_slice(include_bytes!(
            "../../tests/fixtures/qwen3_6_35b_a3b_config.json"
        ))
        .unwrap();
        QWEN3_6_35B_A3B
            .check_config(config.to_string().as_bytes())
            .unwrap();
        // Main tolerates a stray intermediate_size on a MoE family: only the dense arm reads
        // it, and rejecting it here would change what main accepts.
        config["text_config"]["intermediate_size"] = json!(17408);
        QWEN3_6_35B_A3B
            .check_config(config.to_string().as_bytes())
            .unwrap();
    }
}
//! Crate-internal executor seam: the `ExecutorOps` trait and the per-job `GenerationState`.
//!
//! The scripted test fake lives in `crate::exec_fake`.

use crate::EngError;
use crate::family::sampler::Sampler;
use crate::family::session::{SaveKind, StoreLimits};
use crate::sched::job::PrefixReport;
use crate::tokenizer::{DecodeBatch, IncrementalDecoder};
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool;

type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, EngError>;

/// Per-job generation state. The executor feeds the decoder inside `decode`.
pub(crate) struct GenerationState {
    pub(crate) decoder: IncrementalDecoder,
    pub(crate) cancel: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    /// The sampler of this job. The executor draws from it inside `decode`.
    pub(crate) sampler: Sampler,
    /// The output limit of this job. `None` means the job has no limit of its own.
    max_tokens: Option<u32>,
    /// The tokens that count toward `max_tokens`. An EOS token does not count.
    generated: u32,
}

impl GenerationState {
    /// Creates the state of one job with an unset cancellation flag and a greedy sampler.
    pub(crate) fn new(decoder: IncrementalDecoder) -> Self {
        Self::with_sampler(decoder, Sampler::greedy())
    }

    /// Creates the state of one job with an unset cancellation flag and the given sampler.
    pub(crate) fn with_sampler(decoder: IncrementalDecoder, sampler: Sampler) -> Self {
        Self {
            decoder,
            cancel: Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false)),
            sampler,
            max_tokens: None,
            generated: 0,
        }
    }

    /// Sets the output limit of this job. A limit of zero ends the job on its first `decode` call.
    pub(crate) fn with_max_tokens(mut self, max_tokens: u32) -> Self {
        self.max_tokens = Some(max_tokens);
        self
    }

    /// Returns the tokens the job can still generate, or `None` when the job has no limit.
    pub(crate) fn remaining_tokens(&self) -> Option<u32> {
        self.max_tokens
            .map(|limit| limit.saturating_sub(self.generated))
    }

    /// Counts `count` generated tokens against the limit. Never count an EOS token.
    pub(crate) fn record_generated(&mut self, count: u32) {
        self.generated = self.generated.saturating_add(count);
    }
}

/// The calls the engine worker makes on an executor, in the worker's call order. `check_prompt`
/// comes first: the worker asks it at the start of every job, before it resets a session or
/// feeds a token, so a prompt that cannot fit is refused before any engine work.
pub(crate) trait ExecutorOps {
    type Session;
    /// The admitted simultaneous sessions. Existing executors keep their single-session path.
    fn max_seqs(&self) -> usize {
        1
    }
    /// Allocates independent mutable state on this executor's engine thread.
    fn new_session(&mut self) -> Result<Self::Session> {
        Err(EngError::BadRequest(
            "this executor does not support independent batch sessions".into(),
        ))
    }
    /// Advances a row-ordered window. Outer errors invalidate every affected session; inner
    /// errors refuse only that row before its feed. A Backend error at either level is terminal
    /// before any publication. This default never simulates batching.
    fn decode_window(
        &mut self,
        _sessions: &mut [&mut Self::Session],
        _generations: &mut [&mut GenerationState],
    ) -> Result<Vec<Result<DecodeBatch>>> {
        Err(EngError::BadRequest(
            "this executor does not support decode windows".into(),
        ))
    }
    /// An executor with a context limit returns the typed over-length refusal for a prompt
    /// that cannot fit; it changes no state. Executors without a limit accept every prompt.
    fn check_prompt(&self, _prompt_tokens: usize) -> Result<()> {
        Ok(())
    }
    /// The committed tokens of the session.
    fn history<'s>(&self, st: &'s Self::Session) -> &'s [u32];
    /// Clears all mutable session state together.
    fn reset(&mut self, st: &mut Self::Session) -> Result<()>;
    /// Consumes one non-empty prompt chunk.
    fn prefill(&mut self, st: &mut Self::Session, toks: &[u32]) -> Result<()>;
    /// Commits one batch of tokens, or reports `Cancelled`.
    fn decode(
        &mut self,
        st: &mut Self::Session,
        generation: &mut GenerationState,
    ) -> Result<DecodeBatch>;
    /// Completes deferred work after a batch is sent, before another decode or job reset.
    fn after_emit(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
        Ok(())
    }
    /// Clears transient routing and draft state at a turn boundary.
    fn boundary(&mut self, st: &mut Self::Session);
    /// The number of prompt tokens that one worker piece feeds when this executor plans its own
    /// chunks. The worker refreshes this hint between pieces. `None` means the caller's
    /// fallback; `Some(0)` is invalid and is checked at startup and between pieces.
    fn prefill_piece(&self) -> Option<usize> {
        None
    }
    /// The limits of this executor's prefix store: how many pinned roots and how many LRU entries
    /// it holds. The worker asks once per job and plans its save points with the answer: it emits a
    /// root point only when `roots > 0`, so a job with a root boundary behaves like a job without
    /// one on an engine that keeps no roots. It emits periodic points only when `entries >= 2`,
    /// because with one entry the tip would replace a periodic entry at once. The default is a
    /// store of zero roots and one entry. An executor that enables the set overrides this method
    /// and must answer with the limits of its own store (the Qwen3.6 engine will answer two roots
    /// and six entries).
    fn prefix_limits(&self) -> StoreLimits {
        StoreLimits::default()
    }
    /// The block prefix-match spacing (default ON): `None` only on the fail-safe rollback (a
    /// set value keeps the feature on solely for `1`/`true`/`on`, trimmed and case-folded;
    /// everything else, including non-UTF-8, disables); `Some(tokens)` cuts one rolling
    /// intermediate entry per stored path at the last block boundary below the tip. Each stored
    /// path holds at most one rolling Block. A protected store may retain a recent longer Block
    /// instead of a shorter replacement. The default reads `ENGINESRV_PREFIX_BLOCK_MATCH` and
    /// `ENGINESRV_PREFIX_BLOCK_TOKENS` once; a test fake overrides this to control the spacing
    /// without the environment.
    fn prefix_block_spacing(&self) -> Option<usize> {
        crate::family::session::prefix_block_spacing()
    }
    /// Saves the session as an entry of the engine's prefix store. `kind` names the save point:
    /// `SaveKind::Root` a pinned root at the end of the first system message, `SaveKind::Periodic`
    /// a periodic checkpoint of a long prompt, and `SaveKind::Tip` the last message boundary. `key`
    /// holds the committed prompt tokens of the session. Returns `Ok(false)` when this executor
    /// cannot save or when the memory plan denies the charge. It never changes the session.
    /// Executors that keep no prefix state use this default.
    fn save_prefix(&mut self, _st: &Self::Session, _key: &[u32], _kind: SaveKind) -> Result<bool> {
        Ok(false)
    }
    /// Replaces the reset session with the saved prefix state. It does so only when the saved key is
    /// shorter than `prompt`, equals its first tokens, and comes from the current numeric path.
    /// Returns the number of prompt tokens that the state covers, or 0 with the session unchanged.
    fn restore_prefix(&mut self, _st: &mut Self::Session, _prompt: &[u32]) -> Result<usize> {
        Ok(0)
    }
    /// The prefix-store report of this executor, which the worker takes once per job after the
    /// prefill and carries in `JobUsage`: the entries the store holds, the charged bytes of their
    /// snapshots, the kind of the entry the job restored, and the prompt tokens shared with a
    /// stored key beyond the restored prefix. Executors that keep no prefix report use this
    /// default: `None`, and the request log then omits its four `prefix_*` keys even for a request
    /// with a boundary (no false zeros). The Flash-Next executor keeps this default: it reports
    /// nothing.
    fn prefix_report(&self) -> Option<PrefixReport> {
        None
    }
    /// Evicts ONE of the engine's evictable prefix entries per the incremental denial order: dead
    /// tips first, then redundant single-chain interior anchors, then anchor leaves, then branch
    /// points (a shared header), oldest first within each tier; `protect` (the denied job's
    /// restored anchor) goes last; roots stay pinned. Returns the number of bytes the eviction
    /// released from the session budget, or `None` when no evictable entry remains - the caller's
    /// eviction loop ends there and the denial stands for classification. Executors that keep no
    /// prefix state use this default: nothing to free.
    // shortcut: the freed-byte count is not logged anywhere - the sched worker has no log
    // channel; log it where the server's request log lives when a failing test needs it.
    fn evict_one_prefix_entry(&mut self, _protect: Option<u64>) -> Option<u64> {
        None
    }
    /// The entry the denying session restored, to protect it last in
    /// [`Self::evict_one_prefix_entry`]. Executors that keep no prefix state - or callers
    /// with no session yet, like an admission rebuild - use this default: no protected
    /// lineage.
    fn restored_anchor_of(&self, _st: &Self::Session) -> Option<u64> {
        None
    }
    /// The entry a restart of `prompt` would restore first: an admission-rebuild eviction protects
    /// it, because no session exists there to carry the lineage and the rebuild must not free the
    /// very anchor its next attempt restores. Executors that keep no prefix state use this default:
    /// no candidate.
    fn restore_candidate(&self, _prompt: &[u32]) -> Option<u64> {
        None
    }
    /// The largest prompt, in tokens, that the session budget could still admit for a fresh attempt
    /// of `st`: the pool-derived effective ceiling, not the configured context limit. The worker
    /// reports it as `PromptTooLong::limit_tokens` when an admission cannot be served even after
    /// the eviction, so a client can compact to a size that fits. The ceiling counts the pool's
    /// free bytes plus the bytes `st` itself would release on its next reset, because every attempt
    /// begins from a reset session. `None` means the executor budgets nothing and reports no
    /// ceiling.
    fn pool_prompt_ceiling(&self, _st: &Self::Session) -> Option<u64> {
        None
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{ExecutorOps, GenerationState};
    use crate::EngError;
    use crate::family::sampler::{Sampler, SamplingParams};
    use crate::family::session::{SaveKind, StoreLimits};
    use crate::tokenizer::{DecodeBatch, IncrementalDecoder, Tokenizer};
    use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;

    const TOKENIZER_JSON: &str = r#"{"version":"1.0","truncation":null,"padding":null,"added_tokens":[],"normalizer":null,"pre_tokenizer":{"type":"ByteLevel","add_prefix_space":false,"trim_offsets":false,"use_regex":false},"post_processor":{"type":"ByteLevel","add_prefix_space":false,"trim_offsets":false,"use_regex":false},"decoder":{"type":"ByteLevel","add_prefix_space":false,"trim_offsets":false,"use_regex":false},"model":{"type":"BPE","dropout":null,"unk_token":null,"continuing_subword_prefix":null,"end_of_word_suffix":null,"fuse_unk":false,"byte_fallback":false,"ignore_merges":false,"vocab":{"a":0},"merges":[]}}"#;

    fn new_decoder() -> IncrementalDecoder {
        let tokenizer = Tokenizer::from_bytes(TOKENIZER_JSON.as_bytes()).expect("parse tokenizer");
        IncrementalDecoder::new(&tokenizer)
    }

    fn new_state() -> GenerationState {
        GenerationState::new(new_decoder())
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_helper_builds_a_state_whose_decoder_decodes() {
        let mut state = new_state();
        assert_eq!(state.decoder.push(0).expect("push token 0"), "a");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_new_generation_state_starts_uncancelled_and_owns_its_flag() {
        let first = new_state();
        let second = new_state();
        assert!(!first.cancel.load(Ordering::SeqCst), "first starts set");
        first.cancel.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
        assert!(first.cancel.load(Ordering::SeqCst), "store is lost");
        assert!(
            !second.cancel.load(Ordering::SeqCst),
            "second shares the flag of first"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_new_generation_state_samples_greedily() {
        let mut state = new_state();
        for _ in 0..5 {
            let id = state.sampler.sample(&[0.0, 2.0, 1.0]).expect("sample");
            assert_eq!(id, 1);
        }
    }

    /// An executor that implements only the required calls.
    struct Bare;

    impl ExecutorOps for Bare {
        type Session = Vec<u32>;
        fn history<'s>(&self, st: &'s Vec<u32>) -> &'s [u32] {
            st
        }
        fn reset(&mut self, st: &mut Vec<u32>) -> Result<(), EngError> {
            st.clear();
            Ok(())
        }
        fn prefill(&mut self, st: &mut Vec<u32>, toks: &[u32]) -> Result<(), EngError> {
            st.extend_from_slice(toks);
            Ok(())
        }
        fn decode(
            &mut self,
            _st: &mut Vec<u32>,
            _generation: &mut GenerationState,
        ) -> Result<DecodeBatch, EngError> {
            Err(EngError::BadRequest(
                "bare executor does not decode".to_string(),
            ))
        }
        fn boundary(&mut self, _st: &mut Vec<u32>) {}
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_executor_without_window_support_keeps_solo_defaults() {
        let mut executor = Bare;
        assert_eq!(executor.max_seqs(), 1);
        assert!(matches!(
            executor.new_session(),
            Err(EngError::BadRequest(_))
        ));
        let mut session = vec![1, 2, 3];
        let mut generation = new_state();
        assert!(matches!(
            executor.decode_window(&mut [&mut session], &mut [&mut generation]),
            Err(EngError::BadRequest(_))
        ));
        assert_eq!(session, [1, 2, 3]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_executor_without_prefix_support_saves_nothing_and_restores_nothing() {
        let mut executor = Bare;
        let mut session = vec![1, 2, 3];
        assert!(
            !executor
                .save_prefix(&session, &[1, 2, 3], SaveKind::Tip)
                .expect("save")
        );
        assert_eq!(
            executor
                .restore_prefix(&mut session, &[1, 2, 3, 4])
                .expect("restore"),
            0
        );
        assert_eq!(session, vec![1, 2, 3], "the session is unchanged");
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_executor_without_prefix_support_reports_the_addendum_one_limits() {
        assert_eq!(
            Bare.prefix_limits(),
            StoreLimits {
                roots: 0,
                entries: 1
            },
            "zero roots and one entry (a literal, not the default under test)"
        );
    }

    /// The default `prefix_report` of an executor without a prefix report is `None`: its request
    /// lines omit the four `prefix_*` keys instead of carrying false zeros.
    #[test]
    fn an_executor_without_prefix_support_reports_no_prefix_report() {
        assert_eq!(
            Bare.prefix_report(),
            None,
            "no report, taken with `&self`, after any call sequence"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_generation_state_keeps_the_sampler_it_is_given() {
        let params = SamplingParams::new(1.0, 1.0, 0).expect("params");
        let mut state = GenerationState::with_sampler(new_decoder(), Sampler::new(params, 0));
        let id = state.sampler.sample(&[0.0; 4]).expect("sample");
        assert_eq!(id, 3);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_new_generation_state_has_no_token_limit() {
        let mut state = new_state();
        assert_eq!(state.remaining_tokens(), None, "fresh state");
        state.record_generated(3);
        assert_eq!(
            state.remaining_tokens(),
            None,
            "recording keeps it unlimited"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn with_max_tokens_sets_the_limit_and_keeps_the_sampler() {
        let params = SamplingParams::new(1.0, 1.0, 0).expect("params");
        let mut state = GenerationState::with_sampler(new_decoder(), Sampler::new(params, 0))
            .with_max_tokens(5);
        assert_eq!(state.remaining_tokens(), Some(5), "limit");
        let id = state.sampler.sample(&[0.0; 4]).expect("sample");
        assert_eq!(id, 3, "the sampler given to the state is kept");
    }

    #[test]
    fn recorded_tokens_reduce_the_remaining_limit_and_saturate() {
        let mut state = new_state().with_max_tokens(5);
        state.record_generated(2);
        assert_eq!(state.remaining_tokens(), Some(3), "after two tokens");
        state.record_generated(10);
        assert_eq!(state.remaining_tokens(), Some(0), "past the limit");
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_generated_counter_saturates_instead_of_wrapping() {
        let mut state = new_state().with_max_tokens(5);
        state.record_generated(u32::MAX);
        state.record_generated(2);
        assert_eq!(state.remaining_tokens(), Some(0), "counter does not wrap");
    }
}
//! Files of the Flash-Next artifact directory that the server loads.
//!
//! The artifact manifest (`download-manifest.json`) maps each file name to `{"sha256", "size"}`.
//! The manifest is the authority for the tokenizer files. `TokenizerBundle::load` checks each file
//! against the pin that `tokenizer_pin` builds, so a stepping-stone template cannot load by mistake.

use crate::{EngError, tokenizer::TokenizerPin};
use serde_json::Value;

fn manifest_error(message: String) -> EngError {
    EngError::Checkpoint(format!("artifact manifest: {message}"))
}

/// Reads the SHA-256 of `name` from the parsed manifest.
fn digest(manifest: &Value, name: &str) -> Result<[u8; 32], EngError> {
    let text = manifest
        .get(name)
        .and_then(|entry| entry.get("sha256"))
        .and_then(Value::as_str)
        .ok_or_else(|| manifest_error(format!("no sha256 for {name}")))?;
    if text.len() != 64 {
        return Err(manifest_error(format!("sha256 of {name} is not 64 digits")));
    }
    let mut out = [0u8; 32];
    for (slot, pair) in out.iter_mut().zip(text.as_bytes().as_chunks::<2>().0) {
        let digits = std::str::from_utf8(pair.as_slice())
            .ok()
            .and_then(|digits| u8::from_str_radix(digits, 16).ok())
            .ok_or_else(|| manifest_error(format!("sha256 of {name} is not hexadecimal")))?;
        *slot = digits;
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// Builds the tokenizer pin from the artifact manifest. `vocab_size` is the vocabulary size of
/// `tokenizer.json` with its added tokens (248,077 for the pinned Flash-Next artifact).
pub(crate) fn tokenizer_pin(manifest: &[u8], vocab_size: u32) -> Result<TokenizerPin, EngError> {
    let value: Value =
        serde_json::from_slice(manifest).map_err(|error| manifest_error(error.to_string()))?;
    Ok(TokenizerPin {
        tokenizer_json: digest(&value, "tokenizer.json")?,
        tokenizer_config_json: digest(&value, "tokenizer_config.json")?,
        chat_template_jinja: digest(&value, "chat_template.jinja")?,
        generation_config_json: digest(&value, "generation_config.json")?,
        vocab_size,
    })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::tokenizer_pin;
    use crate::EngError;

    /// The four tokenizer entries of the Mac artifact manifest, with one unrelated entry.
    const MANIFEST: &str = r#"{
        "config.json": {"sha256": "319b334a1abb705acf06035aa0331bcb7c25976ff93a5035b543548738a10824", "size": 183155},
        "tokenizer.json": {"sha256": "0997f410c57a1f4e53b09e4be8f4a172d90edd9564368fb0847030937229b9f3", "size": 12809320},
        "tokenizer_config.json": {"sha256": "b11349aafa7cdc6a320767cf7ceb29ed82f7eda5d65e8e0819e76f0ce947bf27", "size": 17928},
        "chat_template.jinja": {"sha256": "c3cf9e34abf4f9e36c2d72165aa9c132d3e2a725b6c2586aaa3a8af9d7a81041", "size": 8952},
        "generation_config.json": {"sha256": "e70c136c1b78ddc1fb0905bac8e733a4dc448d4f852a5dd75143fffc70be550e", "size": 202}
    }"#;

    #[test]
    fn the_pin_holds_the_manifest_hash_of_each_tokenizer_file() {
        let pin = tokenizer_pin(MANIFEST.as_bytes(), 248_077).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(pin.vocab_size, 248_077);
        assert_eq!(pin.tokenizer_json[..4], [0x09, 0x97, 0xf4, 0x10]);
        assert_eq!(pin.tokenizer_json[28..], [0x72, 0x29, 0xb9, 0xf3]);
        assert_eq!(pin.tokenizer_config_json[..4], [0xb1, 0x13, 0x49, 0xaa]);
        assert_eq!(pin.chat_template_jinja[..4], [0xc3, 0xcf, 0x9e, 0x34]);
        assert_eq!(pin.generation_config_json[..4], [0xe7, 0x0c, 0x13, 0x6c]);
        assert_eq!(pin.generation_config_json[28..], [0x70, 0xbe, 0x55, 0x0e]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_missing_tokenizer_entry_names_the_file() {
        let manifest = MANIFEST.replace("chat_template.jinja", "chat_template.other");
        let error = tokenizer_pin(manifest.as_bytes(), 1)
            .err()
            .expect("the manifest must be rejected");
        assert_eq!(
            error,
            EngError::Checkpoint("artifact manifest: no sha256 for chat_template.jinja".into())
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_short_or_non_hex_hash_is_rejected() {
        let short = MANIFEST.replace("c3cf9e34abf4", "c3cf9e34ab");
        let error = tokenizer_pin(short.as_bytes(), 1)
            .err()
            .expect("the manifest must be rejected");
        assert_eq!(
            error,
            EngError::Checkpoint(
                "artifact manifest: sha256 of chat_template.jinja is not 64 digits".into()
            )
        );
        let bad = MANIFEST.replace("c3cf9e34abf4", "c3cf9e34abzz");
        let error = tokenizer_pin(bad.as_bytes(), 1)
            .err()
            .expect("the manifest must be rejected");
        assert_eq!(
            error,
            EngError::Checkpoint(
                "artifact manifest: sha256 of chat_template.jinja is not hexadecimal".into()
            )
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn text_that_is_not_json_is_rejected() {
        let error = tokenizer_pin(b"not json", 1)
            .err()
            .expect("the manifest must be rejected");
        assert!(
            matches!(&error, EngError::Checkpoint(text) if text.starts_with("artifact manifest: ")),
            "{error:?}"
        );
    }
}
//! Flash-Next DeltaNet decode step (design section "DeltaNet").

use super::math::{expect_len, sigmoid, silu, softplus};
use crate::EngError;
use crate::family::project::Projector;

/// Checked DeltaNet dimensions.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct DeltaShape {
    key_heads: usize,
    key_dim: usize,
    value_heads: usize,
    value_dim: usize,
    conv_kernel: usize,
    hidden: usize,
    eps: f32,
    conv_dim: usize,
    state_len: usize,
    ring_len: usize,
}

impl DeltaShape {
    /// Checks the head counts, widths, kernel, hidden width, and epsilon.
    pub(crate) fn new(
        key_heads: u32,
        key_dim: u32,
        value_heads: u32,
        value_dim: u32,
        conv_kernel: u32,
        hidden: u32,
        eps: f32,
    ) -> Result<Self, EngError> {
        if key_heads == 0 || key_dim == 0 || value_heads == 0 || value_dim == 0 || hidden == 0 {
            return Err(EngError::Checkpoint(
                "delta dimensions must exceed zero".into(),
            ));
        }
        if conv_kernel < 2 {
            return Err(EngError::Checkpoint(
                "delta convolution kernel must be at least 2".into(),
            ));
        }
        if !value_heads.is_multiple_of(key_heads) {
            return Err(EngError::Checkpoint(
                "delta value heads must divide by key heads".into(),
            ));
        }
        if !eps.is_finite() || eps < 0.0 {
            return Err(EngError::Checkpoint("delta epsilon is invalid".into()));
        }
        let kh = key_heads as usize;
        let kd = key_dim as usize;
        let vh = value_heads as usize;
        let vd = value_dim as usize;
        let ck = conv_kernel as usize;
        let (conv_dim, state_len, ring_len) = checked_sizes(kh, kd, vh, vd, ck)
            .ok_or_else(|| EngError::Checkpoint("delta dimensions overflow".into()))?;
        Ok(Self {
            key_heads: kh,
            key_dim: kd,
            value_heads: vh,
            value_dim: vd,
            conv_kernel: ck,
            hidden: hidden as usize,
            eps,
            conv_dim,
            state_len,
            ring_len,
        })
    }

    /// Key heads.
    pub(crate) fn key_heads(&self) -> usize {
        self.key_heads
    }
    /// Width of one key head.
    pub(crate) fn key_dim(&self) -> usize {
        self.key_dim
    }
    /// Value heads.
    pub(crate) fn value_heads(&self) -> usize {
        self.value_heads
    }
    /// Width of one value head.
    pub(crate) fn value_dim(&self) -> usize {
        self.value_dim
    }
    /// Convolution kernel length.
    pub(crate) fn conv_kernel(&self) -> usize {
        self.conv_kernel
    }
    /// Convolution channels `2 * key_heads * key_dim + value_heads * value_dim`.
    pub(crate) fn conv_dim(&self) -> usize {
        self.conv_dim
    }
    /// RMS normalization epsilon.
    pub(crate) fn eps(&self) -> f32 {
        self.eps
    }
}

/// Return
